Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8379-reconcile-redundant-assertion`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and never writes the assignee field.

Small card, and the measurement is already done — the objectui#8342 dev removed the assertion and got `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 with **zero** diagnostics. **Re-measure it on your own base anyway**: `origin/main` has moved several times today, and PR #8377 (the card this fell out of) may or may not have landed by the time you cut.

Two things make this more than a tidy-up, and both belong in the PR body:

- The assertion sits on **exactly the seam objectui#8342 was about**. It is the one that would erase the diagnostic if either side's type is ever tightened — which is precisely how objectui#8342's defect stayed invisible behind `chatResult as any` until someone removed it.
- ⚠️ **A redundant assertion and a load-bearing one look identical.** The whole value here is the proof that it is the former, so the PR must carry it: removal → `type-check` green with the diagnostic count quoted, plus the reverse leg (put it back → still green), so the reader can see the assertion is inert in both directions rather than merely tolerated in one.

⚠️ The instrument is `type-check`, not vitest — vitest transpiles types away. Run **both** projects (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): objectui#8342 measured a case that was red **only** in the test program, because compile-time pins live in `*.test.tsx` files `tsconfig.json` excludes by directory. Prove your files are in the program you are quoting (`--listFiles | grep -c`), with a lit control.

If removal turns out **not** to be clean, that is the more interesting result — report what it holds up and stop; do not widen the PR to chase it.
